subject: terraforming

resources.title: NASA Astrobiology
resources.notes: Use as evidence base for habitability and life-support research, not as proof that planetary-scale terraforming is currently feasible.

resources.title: Planetary Data System Atmospheres Node
resources.notes: Planetary atmosphere observations and mission data.

resources.title: Planetary Data System Geosciences Node
resources.notes: Planetary geology, geochemistry and surface science data.

resources.title: Environmental Control and Life Support Systems
resources.notes: Real spacecraft life-support engineering reference; applicable to habitats, not planetary-scale environmental modification.

resources.title: Life Support Subsystems
resources.notes: NASA JSC reference covering research, analysis, development and testing of open- and closed-loop life-support technologies including atmosphere revitalization, oxygen generation, contaminant control and water recovery. This supports habitat engineering, not claims of planetary terraforming feasibility.

resources.title: Next Generation Life Support (NGLS)
resources.notes: Archived NASA program documenting bioregenerative closed-loop life support and ISRU concepts including crop production, water recovery from Mars regolith, atmospheric oxygen/methane production and dust challenges. Historical technology evidence only; maturity and current applicability must be verified separately.

resources.title: Advanced Plant Habitat
resources.notes: Active ISS plant-growth research facility providing real evidence for controlled-environment plant biology and closed-loop plant support; it does not demonstrate a self-sustaining planetary biosphere.

resources.title: Building Earth-like Planets: From Nebular Gas to Ocean Worlds
resources.notes: Graduate planetary-science curriculum covering differentiation, crust formation, atmospheric degassing, surface-water condensation, volatiles, terrestrial planets, habitability and biosignatures. Provides scientific prerequisites for evaluating habitable environments, not a terraforming recipe.

resources.title: Extrasolar Planets: Physics and Detection Techniques
resources.notes: Quantitative course on exoplanet characterization, temperatures, composition, biosignatures and habitable conditions using real data. Mapped only to the scientific habitability/environment cells relevant to the existing taxonomy.

coverage_notes: Terraforming remains a speculative umbrella subject; mappings represent established enabling sciences and engineering rather than proof that planetary-scale terraforming is feasible.
NASA life-support, plant-habitat and ISRU materials strengthen closed-loop habitat, biosphere, water, regolith and settlement evidence while preserving technology-maturity caveats.
MIT planetary-science courses strengthen habitability, planetary geology, atmosphere, climate and water instruction using only existing taxonomy keys.
Foundation/beginner instruction, radiation-specific engineering curriculum and validated planetary-scale climate intervention remain genuine gaps.
Research references, archives and technology programs do not establish ATLAS expert readiness without retrieval, practical verification, assessment and provenance checks.
